cards.title: __header__
cards.content:
"""Pure-math operations + the OPS registry table.

The four arithmetic functions are deliberately leaf-level (no slate
cross-doc dependencies) so the future DAG solver (#15) can prove it can
walk this doc bottom-up before touching the calculator doc.
"""
from typing import Callable, Dict

# Operations table is built once at import time so @apply_operation can
# look up the chosen op without an if/elif chain in every call.
OPS: Dict[str, Callable[[float, float], float]] = {}
# OPS
# OPS["+"] = lambda a, b: a + b
# OPS["-"] = lambda a, b: a - b
# OPS["*"] = lambda a, b: a * b
# OPS["/"] = lambda a, b: a / b

cards.title: add
cards.prompt: Return a + b. Pure, no side effects.

cards.title: subtract
cards.prompt: Return a - b. Pure, no side effects.

cards.title: multiply
cards.prompt: Return a * b. Pure, no side effects.

cards.title: divide
cards.prompt: Return a / b. If b is zero, raise ZeroDivisionError("Cannot divide by zero") so the caller can handle it cleanly.

cards.title: register_ops
cards.content:
def register_ops() -> None:
    """Populate the global OPS dict with operator mappings."""
    OPS.clear()
    OPS["+"] = add
    OPS["-"] = subtract
    OPS["*"] = multiply
    OPS["/"] = divide
cards.prompt: Populate the global OPS dict (defined in the header) with mappings from operator strings to the matching function: "+" → @add, "-" → @subtract, "*" → @multiply, "/" → @divide. Idempotent — clear OPS before populating so calling twice is safe.

cards.title: apply_operation
cards.content:
def apply_operation(op: str, a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Apply the given operation to two operands.
    
    Args:
        op: The operation symbol (e.g., '+', '-', '*', '/')
        a: First operand
        b: Second operand
        
    Returns:
        The result of applying the operation to the operands
        
    Raises:
        KeyError: If the operation is not registered in OPS
    """
    try:
        return OPS[op](a, b)
    except KeyError:
        raise KeyError(f"Operation '{op}' is not registered") from None
cards.prompt: Look the op up in OPS (defined in the header) and apply it to (a, b). Raise KeyError with a clear message if the op is not registered.

cards.title: __header__
cards.content:
"""Tiny CLI calculator — read two numbers + one op, print the result.

Imports its math kernel from the sibling `operations` doc, which the
slate compiler emits as operations.py at the same destination. This
demonstrates the cross-doc compile pattern: each doc is its own .py file,
and inter-doc deps are plain Python imports.
"""
from operations import OPS, register_ops, apply_operation

cards.title: read_number
cards.prompt: Prompt the user with the given string and re-prompt until they enter a parseable float. Returns the float.

cards.title: read_two_numbers
cards.prompt: Use @read_number twice — once with prompt "Enter the first number: " and once with "Enter the second number: " — and return them as a tuple (a, b).

cards.title: read_operator
cards.prompt: Prompt the user (showing the keys of OPS sorted) until they enter one of the registered operators. Return the operator string. OPS is imported from the operations doc via the header.

cards.title: main
cards.prompt: Entry point. Call @register_ops (cross-doc — from operations), then read inputs via @read_two_numbers and @read_operator, then call @apply_operation (cross-doc — from operations). Print the formatted result. Catch ZeroDivisionError and print an error message instead of crashing. Include `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` at the bottom.
